intro: You are in the Bursa Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts, in Bursa province, opened in 1974. It is set in the madrasa of the Green complex, and inside the students' cells you will find the tiles, metalwork and manuscripts of the Ottomans' founding centuries.
history: The museum opened in 1974 in the restored madrasa of Mehmed I's Green complex. Where students once lived, their cells became display cases. The collection covers the tiles, metalwork and manuscripts of the centuries when Bursa was the Ottoman capital.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the madrasa courtyard and the tile collection. Then take your time with the Ottoman metalwork and the manuscripts.
facts: Did you know? Some of the tiles here are workshop trials for the ones that went into the mosque of the same complex. And the museum itself occupies the madrasa of the Green complex, its students' cells turned into display cases.
outro: Our time in the Bursa Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts ends here. One small request before you go: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these pieces stay safe for the visitors who follow you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
